senses.def: grown or produced without artificial chemicals
examples: Organic vegetables usually cost more at the supermarket.
They run a small organic farm in Vermont.

senses.def: produced by or coming from living things
examples: Compost is made from organic waste like food scraps and leaves.

senses.def: developing naturally and gradually
examples: The company's growth has been slow and organic.

senses.def: a group of people who work together for a particular purpose, such as a business or charity
examples: She works for a nonprofit organization that helps refugees.
The World Health Organization issued a new warning.

senses.def: the act of planning or arranging something, or the way it is arranged
examples: The organization of the conference took months.
His essay is full of good ideas but lacks organization.

note: American spelling with z; British also uses organisation. Trap: an event is not usually called "an organization" in English; say event.

senses.def: connected with an organization or the way it is run
examples: The company went through major organizational changes last year.
Organizational culture affects how happy employees are.

senses.def: connected with planning and arranging things
examples: She has excellent organizational skills.

senses.def: to plan and arrange an event or activity
examples: We're organizing a surprise party for Dad's birthday.
Students organized a protest against the tuition increase.

senses.def: to arrange things in a sensible order or system
examples: I spent Sunday organizing my closet.

senses.def: to form a group such as a labor union
examples: Workers at the warehouse are trying to organize.

senses.def: planned and carried out by a large group of people working together
examples: Police believe the thefts are the work of organized crime.
He isn't a fan of organized religion.

senses.def: able to plan your work and life well, or arranged in a clear way
examples: She's very organized and never misses a deadline.
The report is well organized and easy to follow.

note: Opposite: disorganized. "Get organized" = start planning things properly.

senses.def: a person who plans and arranges an event or activity
examples: The organizers expect 10,000 people at the festival.
She works as a community organizer in Detroit.

senses.def: a container or diary used to keep things in order
examples: I bought a desk organizer for my pens and cables.

senses.def: to aim something at a particular group or purpose
examples: The program is oriented toward first-generation college students.
We need to orient our marketing more to younger customers.

senses.def: to find your position or get used to a new situation
examples: It took me a few days to orient myself in the new city.
He used the mountains to orient himself.

note: Very common in compound adjectives: goal-oriented, family-oriented. British English often uses orientate.

senses.def: a person's basic beliefs, attitudes or interests
examples: It is illegal to discriminate based on sexual orientation.
The party has a strong left-wing orientation.

senses.def: training or information given to people who are new to a place or job
examples: All new employees attend a two-day orientation.
Freshman orientation starts the week before classes.

senses.def: the direction in which something faces
examples: The orientation of the house gives it lots of morning sun.

senses.def: the point where something begins, or the cause of something
examples: Scientists are still debating the origin of the virus.
Many English words have Latin origins.

senses.def: the country, race or social class that a person comes from
examples: She is of Mexican origin.
People of all origins live in this neighborhood.

senses.def: existing at the beginning, before any changes
examples: The original plan was to drive, but we flew instead.
The house still has its original windows.

senses.def: new and interesting, not copied from something else
examples: It's a highly original novel with a surprising ending.

senses.def: the first version of a document or work of art, from which copies are made
examples: Keep the original and send them a photocopy.
The painting in the hall is a copy; the original is in Paris.

senses.def: at the beginning, before something changed
examples: The building was originally a train station.
I'm originally from Ohio, but I live in Texas now.

senses.def: in a new and creative way
examples: The room was decorated very originally.

note: "Where are you originally from?" asks where someone was born or grew up.

senses.def: to start or come from a particular place, time or situation
examples: The tradition originated in Germany in the 16th century.
The fire originated in the kitchen.

senses.def: to create or start something new
examples: Who originated the idea of a four-day workweek?

senses.def: additional, different, or the remaining one(s) of a group
examples: Do you have this shirt in any other colors?
The other students had already left.

senses.def: the remaining or a different person or thing
examples: Some people like summer; others prefer winter.
One twin is shy, but the other is very outgoing.

note: "The other day" = a few days ago. "Every other day" = every second day (gün aşırı). "Other than" = except.

senses.def: used to say what will happen if something is not done or the situation is different
examples: Take an umbrella; otherwise you'll get soaked.
I'm glad you called; otherwise I'd have forgotten.

senses.def: apart from what has just been mentioned
examples: The soup was a little cold, but otherwise the meal was excellent.

senses.def: in a different way
examples: Unless you hear otherwise, the meeting will be at ten.

senses.def: used to say what is the right or sensible thing to do
examples: You ought to apologize to her.
We ought to leave early to avoid the traffic.

senses.def: used to say what you expect to be true or to happen
examples: The package ought to arrive by Friday.

note: Always followed by to: "ought to go". Similar to should but a little more formal. Past: ought to have done (yapmalıydı).

senses.def: belonging to or connected with us
examples: Our apartment is on the third floor.
We had to cancel our vacation because of the storm.

note: Often pronounced the same as "are" /ɑːr/ in American English; also /ˈaʊər/.

senses.def: the one or ones that belong to us
examples: Their house is bigger than ours.
Is this car ours or the neighbors'?

note: No apostrophe: ours, not our's. "A friend of ours" = one of our friends.

senses.def: used when we are both the subject and the object of an action
examples: We really enjoyed ourselves at the party.
We should be proud of ourselves for finishing on time.

senses.def: used to emphasize "we" or "us"
examples: We built the deck ourselves.

note: "By ourselves" = alone or without help.

senses.def: away from the inside of a place, or not at home
examples: She opened the box and took out a letter.
Sorry, he's out right now; can I take a message?

senses.def: no longer available, or no longer burning or shining
examples: We're out of milk, so I'll go to the store.
The lights went out during the storm.

senses.def: (informal) through something to the outside
examples: He looked out the window at the rain.

note: "Look out the window" is American; British English prefers "out of the window". "Be out of something" = have none left.

senses.def: the sudden start of something unpleasant, especially a disease or violence
examples: Health officials are investigating an outbreak of food poisoning.
Thousands fled the region after the outbreak of war.

note: The verb is "break out": "War broke out in 1939".

senses.def: the result or effect of an action, process or event
examples: We're still waiting for the outcome of the election.
Early treatment leads to better outcomes for patients.

senses.def: used, happening or located outside rather than inside a building
examples: The hotel has a heated outdoor pool.
She loves outdoor activities like hiking and kayaking.

note: Outdoor is an adjective before a noun (outdoor café); outdoors is an adverb (eat outdoors). Opposite: indoor.

senses.def: outside, not in a building
examples: The kids played outdoors until it got dark.
In summer we often eat outdoors on the patio.

senses.def: the countryside and nature, away from buildings
examples: He's a lover of the great outdoors.

note: Opposite: indoors.

senses.def: on the outside of something, or far from the center
examples: Remove the outer leaves of the cabbage.
They live in the outer suburbs of the city.

note: Opposite: inner. Used only before a noun.

senses.def: a set of clothes worn together, especially for a particular occasion
examples: She bought a new outfit for the job interview.
I love your outfit; where did you get the jacket?

senses.def: a group of people working together, such as a small company or band
examples: He works for a small software outfit in Seattle.

senses.def: a short trip for pleasure or education, usually with a group
examples: The class went on an outing to the science museum.
A trip to the zoo makes a great family outing.

senses.def: a store that sells a company's goods, often cheaply, or a business that sells or publishes something
examples: We bought cheap sneakers at the outlet mall.
Several news outlets reported the story.

senses.def: a place in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment
examples: Is there an outlet near the desk where I can charge my phone?

senses.def: a way of expressing or releasing strong feelings or energy
examples: Painting is a good outlet for stress.

note: In American English, an electrical outlet is what British people call a socket or power point.

senses.def: a description of the main facts or points of something, without the details
examples: Write a short outline of your essay before you start.
The manager gave us a brief outline of the plan.

senses.def: a line that shows the shape or edge of something
examples: We could see the outline of the mountains against the sky.

senses.def: to describe the main facts or points of something
examples: The governor outlined her plans for the new budget.

senses.def: a person's general attitude to life and the world
examples: Despite her illness, she has a very positive outlook.
Traveling abroad changed his whole outlook on life.

senses.def: what is likely to happen in the future
examples: The economic outlook for next year is uncertain.
The weather outlook for the weekend is sunny.

senses.def: the amount of something that a person, machine or organization produces
examples: The factory doubled its output last year.
Industrial output fell by 3% in March.

senses.def: information produced by a computer or program
examples: Check the output of the program for errors.

senses.def: to produce information or power
examples: The software can output the results as a spreadsheet.

note: Opposite: input. Irregular verb: output – output – output (outputted is also used).

senses.def: a strong feeling of shock and anger
examples: The decision caused public outrage.
Parents expressed outrage at the school's response.

senses.def: an act or event that is very shocking and wrong
examples: It's an outrage that families have to wait years for housing.

senses.def: to make someone very shocked and angry
examples: Fans were outraged by the price of the tickets.

senses.def: not in a building, room or container
examples: Let's eat outside; it's a beautiful day.
Wait outside while I get changed.

senses.def: on or to the outside of something, or not within a particular area or limit
examples: I'll meet you outside the theater at seven.
We live just outside Boston.

senses.def: the outer side or surface of something
examples: The outside of the house needs painting.

senses.def: on the outer side, or coming from beyond a particular group
examples: The company hired an outside consultant to review its finances.

note: "Think outside the box" = think creatively. Americans often say "outside of".

senses.tr: yabancı, dışarıdan biri, grubun dışındaki kişi
senses.def: a person who is not accepted as part of a group or society, or who is not involved in it
examples: As a new kid at school, he felt like an outsider.
To an outsider, the rules of the game seem confusing.

senses.def: a person or team with little chance of winning
examples: She entered the race as a political outsider but won easily.

note: Opposite: insider.

senses.def: extremely good; excellent
examples: She received an award for outstanding achievement in science.
The service at the restaurant was outstanding.

senses.def: not yet paid, done or solved
examples: You have an outstanding balance of $200 on your account.
There are still a few outstanding issues to discuss.

senses.def: the part of a stove, shaped like a box with a door, in which food is baked or heated
examples: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
Take the bread out of the oven before it burns.

note: In the US, the whole appliance is a stove or range; the oven is the box part. A bakery shop is a bakery, not an oven.

senses.def: above something, or covering it
examples: There's a lamp over the dining table.
She put a blanket over the sleeping child.

senses.def: more than, or during a period of time
examples: Over 200 people came to the meeting.
Prices have risen over the past year.

senses.def: finished
examples: The game was over by ten o'clock.

senses.def: across a space, or to a particular place
examples: Come over to my place after work.

note: "Over and over" = again and again. "Get over something" = recover from it.

senses.def: including everything or everyone; general
examples: The overall cost of the project was $2 million.
My overall impression of the city was very positive.

senses.def: in total, or when everything is considered
examples: Overall, I think the trip was a success.
She finished third overall.

note: Overalls (plural noun) = work clothes with a bib and straps (tulum).

senses.def: to succeed in dealing with a problem or difficulty
examples: She overcame her fear of flying with the help of a therapist.
Together we can overcome these challenges.

senses.tr: (duygu, duman vb.) etkisi altına almak, bitap düşürmek
senses.def: to affect someone so strongly that they cannot act or think normally
examples: He was overcome with emotion during his speech.
Two firefighters were overcome by smoke.

note: Irregular: overcome – overcame – overcome.

senses.def: if two things overlap, part of one covers part of the other, or they share some features or time
examples: The two meetings overlap, so I can't attend both.
Our responsibilities overlap in some areas.

senses.def: the amount or part by which things overlap
examples: There is a lot of overlap between the two courses.

note: Stress: verb overLAP, noun OVERlap /ˈəʊvərlæp/.

senses.def: to fail to notice or consider something
examples: The report overlooks some important facts.
It's easy to overlook small errors when you're tired.

senses.def: to choose to ignore a mistake or bad behavior
examples: I'll overlook your lateness this time, but don't let it happen again.

senses.def: to have a view of a place from above
examples: Our hotel room overlooked the harbor.

note: Trap: overlook does NOT mean "oversee" (supervise). It means fail to notice.

senses.def: too much; more than is normal or suitable
examples: I wasn't overly impressed by the new design.
Don't be overly critical of yourself.

note: "Not overly" is a polite understatement: "not overly happy" = rather unhappy.

senses.def: during or for the night
examples: Let the dough rest in the fridge overnight.
We stayed overnight at a motel near the border.

senses.def: very quickly or suddenly
examples: The video made her famous overnight.

senses.def: happening or lasting for one night
examples: She packed an overnight bag for the trip.

note: "An overnight success" = someone who becomes successful very suddenly.

senses.def: in or to a foreign country, especially one across the sea
examples: He spent two years working overseas.
Many graduates move overseas to find better jobs.

senses.def: connected with foreign countries
examples: The university attracts thousands of overseas students.

note: As an adverb, no preposition: "go overseas", not "go to overseas" (same as abroad).

senses.def: to watch and manage a job or activity to make sure it is done correctly
examples: She oversees a team of twenty engineers.
An independent body will oversee the election.

note: Irregular: oversee – oversaw – overseen. Oversight means both "supervision" and "a mistake from not noticing".

senses.def: to officially change a legal decision so that it is no longer valid
examples: The Supreme Court overturned the lower court's ruling.
His conviction was overturned on appeal.

senses.def: to turn over or make something turn over so that its top is at the bottom or side
examples: A truck overturned on the highway, blocking two lanes.

senses.def: to have such a strong emotional effect on someone that they cannot think or act normally
examples: She was overwhelmed by all the kind messages.
Don't let the workload overwhelm you; take it one step at a time.

senses.tr: ezmek, alt etmek, kaldıramayacağı kadar yüklenmek
senses.def: to defeat someone completely, or to be too much for a system to deal with
examples: Hospitals were overwhelmed with patients during the flu season.

note: "I feel overwhelmed" is a very common way to say you have too much to deal with.

senses.def: very great or very strong; too strong to resist or deal with
examples: The proposal won the overwhelming support of voters.
Starting a new job in a new city can be overwhelming.

senses.def: to have to pay back money that you borrowed or pay for something you received
examples: I still owe my brother $50.
How much do I owe you for the tickets?

senses.def: to feel that you should do something for someone, or to have something because of someone
examples: You owe me an apology.
She owes her success to her parents' support.

note: "I owe you one" (informal) = thanks, I'll return the favor. "Owing to" = because of (formal).

senses.def: used after a possessive to emphasize that something belongs to a particular person
examples: I'd love to have my own room.
She runs her own business from home.

senses.def: used to mean something belonging to a particular person
examples: The apartment isn't rented; it's their own.
He moved out and got a place of his own.

senses.def: to have something that belongs to you, especially because you bought it
examples: They own a small house near the lake.

note: "On my own" = alone or without help. "Own up to something" = admit a mistake.

senses.def: a person who owns something
examples: The owner of the restaurant greeted us at the door.
Dog owners must keep their pets on a leash in the park.
